children.name: Real Numbers
children.summary: Number systems, Euclid's algorithm, and properties of real numbers.

exercises.question: Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational.
exercises.solution: Assume sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms. Then 2q^2 = p^2, so p is even. Write p = 2k => 2q^2 = 4k^2 => q^2 = 2k^2, so q is even. Contradiction. Therefore sqrt(2) is irrational.

exercises.question: Show that between any two rational numbers there exists an irrational number.
exercises.solution: Given rationals a < b, choose x = a + (b - a) / sqrt(2). Then x is irrational and lies between a and b.

children.name: Polynomials
children.summary: Polynomial operations, zeroes, and algebraic identities.

exercises.question: If p(x) is a polynomial with p(2)=0, show that (x-2) is a factor of p(x).
exercises.solution: By the Factor Theorem, if p(2)=0 then (x-2) divides p(x).

children.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
children.summary: Solve linear systems using substitution, elimination, and graphical methods.

exercises.question: Solve the system x + y = 5 and 2x - y = 1.
exercises.solution: Add equations to eliminate y: 3x = 6, so x = 2. Then y = 3.

children.name: Physics

children.name: Light - Reflection and Refraction
children.summary: Reflection, refraction, lenses, and mirrors with ray diagrams and laws of optics.

exercises.question: A concave mirror forms a real image at a distance equal to its focal length. Where is the object placed?
exercises.solution: For a concave mirror, when object distance u = f, the image forms at infinity. Therefore the object is at the focus.

exercises.question: Calculate the total resistance of three resistors 2Ω, 3Ω and 6Ω in parallel.

children.name: Chemistry

exercises.question: Balance the equation: Fe + O2 -> Fe2O3.

children.name: Periodic Classification of Elements
children.summary: Modern periodic table, periodic trends, and element groups.

exercises.question: Explain why atomic radius decreases across a period.
exercises.solution: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while electron shielding stays roughly constant, pulling electrons closer and reducing atomic radius.

children.name: Biology

children.name: Life Processes
children.summary: Nutrition, respiration, transportation, and excretion in plants and animals.

exercises.question: Describe the process of transpiration in plants.
exercises.solution: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through stomata. It helps in nutrient transport and cooling the plant.

children.name: Control and Coordination
children.summary: Nervous system, hormones, and plant responses.

exercises.question: What is the role of the endocrine system in coordination?
exercises.solution: The endocrine system secretes hormones that regulate growth, metabolism, and homeostasis, acting alongside the nervous system.

ragEntries.content: NCERT Class X mathematics with foundation topics, theorems, and solved exercises. Chapters: Real Numbers, Polynomials, Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables.

Number systems, Euclid's algorithm, and properties of real numbers. Topics: Euclid's Division Lemma, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Irrational Numbers, Decimal Representations. Exercise examples include proving sqrt 2 is irrational and finding an irrational number between two rationals.
Polynomial operations, zeroes, and algebraic identities. Topics: Degree of Polynomial, Zeroes of Polynomial, Remainder Theorem, Factor Theorem. Includes factor theorem exercise with p(2)=0.

ragEntries.path: Mathematics > Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
ragEntries.content: Solve linear systems using substitution, elimination, and graphical methods. Topics: Graphical Method, Substitution Method, Elimination Method, Applications in Word Problems. Example question solves x + y = 5 and 2x - y = 1.
Class X science syllabus with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology chapters covering optics, electricity, chemical reactions, periodic classification and life processes.

ragEntries.path: Science > Physics > Light - Reflection and Refraction
ragEntries.content: Reflection, refraction, lenses, and mirrors with ray diagrams and laws of optics. Topics include Laws of Reflection, Spherical Mirrors, Refraction, Lenses and Lens Formula. Example exercise asks where an object is placed for a real image at focal length.

Current, resistance, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, and heating effects. Topics include Electric Current, Ohm's Law, Resistance, Series and Parallel Combinations. Exercise calculates equivalent parallel resistance.

ragEntries.path: Science > Chemistry > Chemical Reactions and Equations
ragEntries.content: Types of chemical reactions, balancing equations, and activity series. Topics: Types of Reactions, Balancing Chemical Equations, Endothermic and Exothermic Reactions. Example exercise balances Fe + O2 -> Fe2O3.

ragEntries.path: Science > Chemistry > Periodic Classification of Elements
ragEntries.content: Modern periodic table, periodic trends, and element groups. Topics: Periodic Properties, Atomic Number and Mass Number, Groups and Periods. Example exercise explains why atomic radius decreases across a period.
Nutrition, respiration, transportation, and excretion in plants and animals. Topics include Nutrition, Respiration, Transportation, Excretion. Example exercise describes transpiration.
Nervous system, hormones, and plant responses. Topics include Nervous System, Hormones, Plant Tropisms. Example exercise covers the role of the endocrine system.
